en: One fascicle of the Extremely Profound and Secret Gate of the Vajraśekhara Yoga Trailokyavijaya Sādhana.
By Kai-fu Yi-tong San-si Te-jin Shi Hong-lu Qing, Duke of Su State.
I take refuge in the holy Lord, Samantabhadra Vajrapāṇi, who,
for the sake of subduing all, manifests in the form of Hūṃkāra to destroy the poisons of the three times and cause the immediate realization of bodhi.
This is the profound secret, the King of Reality who is the foremost of the Trailokyavijaya-yoga.
Prostrate to the Samantabhadra-mudrā of purity, union, destruction, entry, and confinement;
place it upon the heart and recite the fundamental vow.
Upon uttering these words, one’s body becomes identical [to the deity].
One performs the four mudrās of Trailokyavijaya-vajra, followed by the jewel initiation, the garland, and the armor.
With the two hands joined and clapped together like a vajra, one immediately enters samādhi.
Contemplate the letter A within the heart; it becomes a moon or sun disc, from which arises a five-pronged vajra of the five wisdoms.
Next, invite the Honored One and the Buddhas to enter and empower the body through samādhi. Furthermore, according to the fundamental teachings...
Having completed the four mudrās, with the five jewel garlands and cymbal-clapping,
one performs the outer and inner offerings. Having finished the hymns of praise,
if one is performing the rite of full ordination (*upasampadā*), one accomplishes the body through the five aspects.
Furthermore, with the fundamental vow of Samantabhadra, [employ] the four wrathful mudrās, the five Buddha jewel-garlands,
the armor, the slapping, and so forth; by means of the Hūṃkāra mudrā method,
[visualize] fire like a lotus, and [perform] the wind-pushing of the karma-fire construction.
The four seals of the forehead, throat, and crown;
within the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, the Great King of Teachings,
the four Buddhas of the Vajradhātu are likewise endowed with these four seals— the mantra of the Vajra Buddha.
The Ratna-vajra and the remaining three [mudrās] follow this principle.
The garland and armor mudrās follow the previous [instructions]. The mantra for the garland is: Oṃ vajramāle nṛtya. To don the armor, recite this vidyā-mantra.
The four means of attraction and the eight offerings are performed according to the ritual of the Vajradhātu;
they appear only in the *niccha* [rite]. The mantra of the hook (*aṅkuśa*) is:
Oṃ hūṃ jaḥ śamaya kuru dhakṣaya sa mañju hūṃ jaḥ phaṭ. The mantra of the noose (*pāśa*) is: [Oṃ hūṃ jaḥ śamaya kuru dhakṣaya sa mañju hūṃ jaḥ phaṭ].
Oṃ vajrapāśamahākrodhagarjite svāhā hūṃ hūṃ. The mantra of the noose is:
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśamahākrodhagarjite svāhā vaṃ. The mantra of the bell is: Oṃ vajraghaṇṭa mahākrodhagarjite svāhā bhrūṃ.
Oṃ vajravesamahe-krodha-kāśaya-saṃghāṭe hūṃ. The mantra for play (*hikṣī*) is as follows:
Furthermore, from the body of the previously visualized wisdom-being, the syllable *A* flows forth from one’s own mind;
before [the practitioner], it becomes a moon disc, from which a vajra is immediately produced.
Five peaks flow with fierce flames; The arising of the three joys is my joy.
Furthermore, regarding the Bhagavān, He immediately summons the Buddhas filling space into the Vajra-lock Joy.
Again, he utters the words "Manifest Clarity."
The Vajra immediately transforms into the wrathful deity Hūṃkāravajra,
seated upon a lunar disc; his body emits a mass of blazing fire,
his entire form is dark blue in color, and he is the Great Lord Maheśvara.
The consort Umā serves as the seat; clearly and distinctly one sees her, empowered by the four mudrās.
Furthermore, the Karmamudrā is shown, and having completed the five empowerments such as the full moon, the jewel garland, the armor, and the cymbals.
Offering internal and external worship, one abides in the body of the Sattva,
brandishes the vajra, and causes the great trichiliocosm to tremble;
reciting the hymn of the One Hundred and Eight Names, one universally invites all the holy sages.
Summoning with the hook, drawing in with the noose, binding with the chain, and gladdening with the bell—these four clarities summon the wisdom-body; entering one's own essence, they are non-dual.
Furthermore, there are the four additions: showing, promising, fulfilling, and the full moon, which constitute the five empowerments.
Having struck with the jewel-garland and finger-cymbals, and having again presented the inner and outer offerings,
he rises and stands with his body straight. Raising his right foot and circling counter-clockwise,
he subdues those who are arrogant— the Great Lord, King of Desire.
Having struck her down to the ground, he firmly presses upon her crown;
with his wisdom-foot he treads upon the breast of the Queen Consort, Umā,
in order to crush her pride, placing his foot upon her head.
Once one has been harmed and perished here, and while dwelling in this samādhi within the realm adorned with ashes,
if one forcefully and repeatedly stamps the body or the body shakes and emits impurities,
one should know that the Honored One is accepting one.
Forming the Samādhi-Wisdom Vajra Fist mudrā at the second stage,
perform the contemplation of the body’s marks and signs while visualizing the wind; when these appear as clearly as before,
rotate [the visualization] and recite the Pādāṅkuśa (Foot-Hook) mantra as follows:
Oṃ kanakarcā vajra hūṃ. At the time of treading with the short step, the mantra is as follows:
Furthermore, one sees the moon in one’s own heart, within which is the Vajra possessing five peaks;
therein resides the vidyā-mantra, emitting blazing vajra-fire.
Abiding in this great samādhi, one should hold the root mantra or the single-syllable heart-vidyā, or the *karmahṛdaya-hṛdaya* Takkirāja mantra;
having thus remained in meditative absorption until one is utterly exhausted.
While seated, recite praises, present offerings, and make aspirations;
then perform the rite of liberation by drawing apart the four locations with the four seals of the root method. The mantra for the heart is as follows:
Furthermore, with the True King, open it by means of the four seals.
The heart-mantra is as follows:
Once the Noble Assembly has returned to their palace, one immediately [performs] the jewel-garland and the finger-cymbals.
Protect this eternal body; the four prostrations, five directions, and so forth are all the same as in other teachings.
For the Trailokyavijaya Yoga, form the two-hand mudrā at the heart; the wisdom hand holds a five-pronged [vajra].
The arms are extended downward as if to strike; next, the arrow and sword are held upright and steady.
Next, the five-pronged hook is held, followed by the bow and the noose, both drawn straight back with the arms extended. All four faces are a pure blue color.
The right side is yellow and the left is green; behind them is red, representing the wrathful consorts of the Heavenly Kings. Their seats are as previously described.
For Hūṃkāra-vajra, one should visualize him with such marks and signs of excellence.
One Scroll of the Extremely Profound and Secret Gate of the Accomplishment of Trailokyavijaya Vajrayoga.
